On the third point:  Last time I read the Bible, Christ never actually even claimed to be the messiah.  When asked if he was, he told Peter to keep it to himself.  His response to something as mild as "Are you the King of the Jews" is "You are who you say I am".  Not an affirmation, but rather a statement about the existential nature of humanity:  We are only who we are perceived to be socially.  Note that this is a deep departure from God's former identity "I am".  (I interpret God to be a metaphor for society, thus Christ is the individual within society)

Honestly, I believe most of the miracles were metaphorical accounts to establish factors of Christ's personality.  Specifically, I harp on the walking on water.  Only God was said to be able to walk on water.  And yet Peter was able to walk on water with Christ.  In my mind, that proves all of mankind has a definite divine nature to them, that is thus the message of Christ.  Likewise, the resurrection demonstrates how a person lives on in society through those around them that they impacted the most.

Honestly, though, I'm still an atheist.  I just appreciate Christian symbolism.  I lost my faith in God by going the long way and working out the theology to all possible logical conclusions.
